incidents.title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
incidents.summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, says criminals are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Scammers have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of Leal offering immigration services he never provides, such as securing US residency for $2,200 or helping detainees escape immigration detention. He discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office about services he never advertised.

The fraud has escalated dramatically over the past three months, with scammers directing victims through WhatsApp after viewing fake social media videos. Leal's office hired an anti-piracy company that removed nearly 6,500 fraudulent profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. He warns immigrants to be cautious of requests for payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App, and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scams. Leal urges people to verify anyone offering legal services online before providing payment.

incidents.title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
incidents.summary:
A fake online article claiming Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock had a heated confrontation with ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler over an unlicensed cryptocurrency platform called Boulder Sparhaven never actually occurred. The article was part of an increasingly common scam that uses artificial intelligence to create convincing false content featuring prominent Australians. Australian Securities and Investments Commission research reveals these sophisticated schemes are becoming more prevalent and harder to detect, with scammers building entire fake online ecosystems including fabricated news articles, reviews, and advertisements.

Last year, ASIC removed 19,400 scams overall, a 182 percent increase from the previous year. The regulator took down 5,476 phishing scams and 7,051 fake investment platforms, representing respective increases of 279 percent and 151 percent. Alan Kohler ranks among the most commonly impersonated Australians, alongside Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, various politicians, and wealthy figures including Gina Rinehart. ASIC advises consumers to verify financial services licenses and check company details through its free public registers before investing, warning that professional-looking content does not guarantee legitimacy.

incidents.title: Sleep Staging Is Not Guesswork
incidents.summary:
A class-action lawsuit has been filed against Oura, the smart ring company, by Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco. The suit alleges that Oura falsely advertised its products' sleep-tracking abilities, claiming the rings can detect sleep stages with 95 percent accuracy comparable to clinical sleep labs. The lawsuit argues that Oura's devices, priced at $300 and up, actually rely on unreliable artificial intelligence guesses rather than the physiological sensors necessary to measure sleep stages accurately. The company built an $11 billion business on these claims, according to the lawsuit.

Oura disputes the allegations, stating it stands behind its science and research. The company says its rings estimate sleep stages using multiple physiological signals including heart rate, heart rate variability, movement, breathing patterns, and temperature. It notes the rings are not medical devices and has been validated against polysomnography in multiple studies. It remains unclear what compensation affected customers might receive if the lawsuit proceeds to trial or reaches a settlement. This marks another legal challenge for Oura, which is already facing a separate class-action lawsuit over alleged unauthorized collection of personal information.

incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi virtual machine environments. The group operates a data leak site and has victimized organizations across multiple countries. Researchers found that Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation attacks against ten target organizations between April and May 2026. The ESXi ransomware uses ChaCha20 encryption and includes an ESXi-specific mode that kills running virtual machines to access their disk files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can read ransom demands.

In a separate operation, researchers identified a second Aurora cluster with medium confidence, affecting eight victim organizations across Israel, Germany, Austria, Spain, the United States, and Argentina. This cluster used different techniques including SQL Server exploitation, privilege escalation with GodPotato, and data exfiltration to S3-compatible storage. Gambit Security provided technical indicators of compromise and details about Aurora's infrastructure, including command and control servers, proxy servers, and the group's onion site for victim negotiations.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
A major Pizza Hut franchisee filed a lawsuit in Texas on May 6, claiming the company's rollout of an AI-powered delivery system called Dragontail caused cascading problems that resulted in over $100 million in damages. Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut locations across the Northeast, alleges the system gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, causing drivers to wait up to 15 minutes to batch multiple orders together rather than delivering pizzas immediately. The franchisee says this practice led to cold, late deliveries and damaged customer satisfaction.

Before Dragontail launched in 2024, Chaac maintained over 90% on-time deliveries and double-digit sales growth. After implementation, the company experienced sharp declines in delivery performance and sales, with year-over-year sales in New York City dropping from positive 10.19% to negative 9.78%. Chaac claims Pizza Hut failed to provide adequate training, ignored requests for support, and continued mandating the system despite worsening metrics. The franchisee is seeking over $100 million in damages plus attorney fees. Pizza Hut stated it is reviewing the claims and will respond through legal channels.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
Scammers are impersonating Terry Gross and other "Fresh Air" staff members to defraud public figures. Authors, entertainers and other professionals have received highly personalized emails claiming to offer interview opportunities on the popular NPR program. The messages include detailed references to the target's work and appear to come from legitimate production staff. History professor Jennifer Black from Misericordia University initially felt excited about receiving such an invitation but became suspicious when asked to pay $250 for production costs, something the legitimate program never requires.

WHYY, NPR and the "Fresh Air" production team confirmed they are aware of these fraudulent emails and are investigating with law enforcement. Cybersecurity experts attribute the scams' effectiveness to artificial intelligence, which allows criminals to personalize impersonations convincingly and inexpensively. Similar scams have targeted other public figures including comedians and journalists. Red flags include payment requests, use of Gmail addresses, and unrealistic scenarios like a famous host personally handling logistics. Experts recommend verifying suspicious requests by contacting the organization directly through legitimate channels rather than responding to the suspicious email.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Israeli officials established a fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute for Public Policy, funded through intermediary companies, to influence artificial intelligence systems toward pro-Israel messaging. Between August 6 and 14, the website published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words designed to appear as neutral academic research addressing controversial topics like genocide allegations and Palestinian expulsions. The operation employed specialized AI optimization techniques to ensure chatbots would cite the content, with all reports formatted as questions users might ask AI systems. The scheme was registered with the US Justice Department as a foreign agent operation, violating transparency requirements.

The broader campaign, financed through tens of millions of dollars and coordinated by European advertising firm Havas Media, involved multiple American contractors including firms connected to former Trump campaign manager Brad Parscale. Israeli government records show substantial unaccounted funding during the campaign period, while officials privately acknowledged the operation failed to improve Israel's declining public approval in America. Experts warn the project demonstrates how foreign governments increasingly manipulate AI training data and chatbot responses, a concerning development with implications beyond this specific case.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels, including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, and others, have filed separate lawsuits against Udio and Suno, two popular artificial intelligence music generators. The labels accuse both companies of scraping massive amounts of copyrighted music without permission or compensation to train their AI models. The lawsuits claim that these companies not only illegally used existing recordings but also directly reproduce sections of famous songs in their generated music. The record labels argue that Udio and Suno have been deliberately unclear about what content they copied and that admitting the truth would reveal widespread copyright infringement.

As part of the lawsuits, the record labels submitted thousands of copyrighted works they claim were used for training, including music from The Beatles, Michael Jackson, Bruce Springsteen, and many others. The labels demonstrated their case by using specific prompts to generate songs that closely replicate famous recordings, including near-identical versions of Green Day's American Idiot and Mariah Carey's All I Want for Christmas Is You. The companies previously claimed their use of copyrighted material constituted fair use. Udio was sued in New York, while Suno was sued in Massachusetts, and these cases are expected to set important precedents for how generative AI services can legally use existing creative works.

incidents.summary:
# Summary

Universal Music Group has settled a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio by reaching licensing agreements. UMG had accused Udio of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence system, including The Temptations' "My Girl." Under the settlement, Udio will launch a new platform next year trained only on authorized and licensed music, allowing users to create, customize, and share songs. The financial terms were not disclosed, though UMG stated the agreements reflect their commitment to supporting artists while embracing new technologies and developing new business models.

Udio, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees, enables users to create original music from text prompts using AI. The startup has attracted millions of users since launching and counts music artist will.i.am and venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz among its backers. This marks Udio's first licensing agreement with a major music label, and artists participating in the new platform will receive compensation, though specific details remain undisclosed. UMG also announced a separate partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
# Summary

State Farm's defense lawyers apologized after their legal filings in a Los Angeles lawsuit contained artificial intelligence-generated fake cases, nonexistent quotes, and false legal holdings. The lawsuit involves homeowner Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, who sued State Farm and others after a 2020 fire made her Carson home uninhabitable. While repairs were underway, storm damage occurred, and Meni-Siliga claims State Farm delayed approving repairs, leaving her work incomplete. She and her husband depleted savings, retirement accounts, declared bankruptcy, and lost their home to foreclosure. A lawyer named Jacquelene Robinson admitted to using an AI tool called Irys, believing it performed citation checks when it did not, resulting in seven fake case citations across eight filings.

The case highlights growing concerns about AI in law, with 41 percent of law firms and 47 percent of corporate legal departments using generative AI. A Paris-based database has documented 1,922 legal hallucination cases worldwide, mostly in the United States. Last year, a California attorney faced a record $10,000 fine for using ChatGPT in a brief containing 21 fabricated quotes. State Farm's lead counsel Kenneth Katel accepted responsibility for the filings and said his firm updated its AI policies. The case is scheduled for trial in October.

stories.Headline: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia Extend Partnership in AI and Data
stories.Summary:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to deepen their cooperation in artificial intelligence, data governance, and emerging technologies. The agreement was announced following a meeting between Pakistan's Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja and Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority President Abdullah bin Sharaf Alghamdi at the LEAP 2026 conference in Riyadh. The two nations plan to establish a comprehensive and long-term technology partnership.

During the discussion, Pakistan's minister outlined the country's national AI and data governance initiatives while reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to building a strong data ecosystem and growing its digital economy. Both countries intend to collaborate on emerging technologies and create a lasting framework for cooperation. The partnership reflects a broader regional focus on advancing artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, technology skills, and data-driven development.

stories.Headline: Mark Cuban Foundation and Tonic Bring Free AI Bootcamp to Denver Teens
stories.Summary:
The Mark Cuban Foundation and Tonic are offering a free artificial intelligence bootcamp to high school students in Denver this fall. The program is open to ninth through twelfth graders and will run over three consecutive Saturdays on October 31, November 7, and November 14. All costs including meals, transportation, and technology will be covered for participants at no charge. Applications close on September 30.

The bootcamp provides hands-on experience with AI tools and explores real-world applications across fields like healthcare, business, sports science, and career preparation. Students will work on a capstone project guided by industry mentors. This Denver bootcamp is one of more than 35 similar programs being hosted across the United States by various companies. Mark Cuban emphasized the importance of providing AI education to underserved students to prepare them for future educational and employment opportunities.

stories.Headline: Datametrex Plans to Focus on AI, Data Centre, and Patent Licensing
stories.Summary:
Datametrex AI Limited announced plans to shut down its healthcare operations to focus on artificial intelligence, data centre technology, and patent licensing. The company operates medical clinics in Edmonton, Calgary, and Vancouver, British Columbia, providing primary and emergency care services. The gradual wind-down aims to streamline the corporate structure, reduce operating costs and regulatory requirements, and improve financial performance by redirecting resources toward core business areas.

The company will manage the transition carefully, considering operational, financial, contractual, and regulatory factors. Management plans to assess opportunities to maximize value from healthcare assets during the process. The strategic shift allows Datametrex to concentrate capital and resources on artificial intelligence and data centre initiatives, which align with long-term objectives. The company indicated it would provide further updates as developments occur.

stories.Headline: Roundup: Chinese AI gaining popularity in Kenya for affordability, performance, customization
stories.Summary:
Chinese artificial intelligence models are becoming increasingly popular among Kenyan developers and technology companies due to their affordability, strong performance, and customizable open-source design. According to recent data, Chinese AI models represented roughly half of AI use on OpenRouter, up from less than 25 percent a year prior, and accounted for 19 of the 25 most-downloaded open-source systems on Hugging Face. Kenyan companies are adopting Chinese models like DeepSeek and Qwen for applications including legal technology, business intelligence, and document processing.

Local technology leaders highlight that Chinese models consume fewer computing resources than Western alternatives while delivering comparable or superior performance, making them practical for Kenya's limited GPU supply. The open-weight nature of these models allows developers to customize them for local languages and African-specific needs without building systems from scratch. Companies like JibuDocs and Qhala are already leveraging these models for innovative applications, while experts suggest potential uses in healthcare diagnostics and disaster prevention could serve underserved African communities.

stories.Headline: Oklahoma State University adds new AI, logistics programs for fall semester
stories.Summary:
Oklahoma State University Institute of Technology is launching two new academic programs beginning in fall 2026. The first is a 60-credit-hour online Associate in Applied Science in Logistics and Supply Chain Technology that students can complete in four to five semesters. This program covers warehousing, transportation, inventory management, and data-informed decision-making, preparing graduates for careers as logistics coordinators, distribution center managers, inventory specialists, and supply chain coordinators. The second offering is an Applied Artificial Intelligence option within the existing Bachelor of Technology in Information Technologies program.

The university designed both programs to address workforce demands in Oklahoma and beyond. The logistics program prepares students for industry-recognized credentials that can lead to over 11 million jobs nationwide. The artificial intelligence program goes beyond teaching tool usage, instead focusing on applying AI technologies to solve real organizational problems while considering ethics and governance. OSUIT Provost Dr. Richie Roberts stated that preparing students with skills aligned to industry needs helps build a strong workforce supporting the state's economic growth.

stories.Headline: Ghana: Ai Will Enhance, Not Replace Surveyors - Ghis President
stories.Summary:
Emmanuel K. Cobbold, president of the Ghana Institution of Surveyors, addressed members at the organization's 57th Founder's Day Anniversary Celebration in Accra. He encouraged surveyors to adopt artificial intelligence and emerging technologies rather than viewing them as threats to their profession. Cobbold emphasized that while AI can assist with measurements, data analysis, and interpretation, professional surveying still requires human judgment, local expertise, and ethical responsibility. He warned that surveyors who fail to adapt to technological changes risk becoming obsolete as the profession evolves.

The institution is working to help members upgrade their skills to meet changing technological demands while maintaining professional integrity standards. Sarah Esi Ziddah, the organization's chief executive officer, noted that surveyors have significantly contributed to Ghana's development, including providing geospatial data during a boundary dispute with Côte d'Ivoire and supporting construction of an infectious disease center. The event brought together current and former members to recognize contributions to the profession and strengthen professional connections among the organization's widely dispersed membership.

stories.Headline: Environmental News Network - AI Project Led by UH Aims to Protect Hawaiʻi's Coastal Freshwater
stories.Summary:
The University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa is launching an artificial intelligence project to forecast threats to coastal freshwater supplies and ecosystems. Associate Professor Jonghyun Lee received a $500,000 grant from the National Science Foundation to lead the initiative, which is part of a broader three-year collaborative effort worth nearly $1 million involving the University of Texas at Austin. The project aims to develop AI applications in geoscience to better understand environmental challenges.

Rising ocean levels, intensified storms, saltwater infiltration of freshwater sources, and coastal ecosystem damage present growing dangers to communities throughout the region. These threats directly endanger drinking water availability, farming operations, infrastructure, and the economic wellbeing of millions of people who depend on coastal areas.
